title: AirLLM Layer-Wise Disk Offloading, Per-Expert MoE Streaming & On-GPU Packed Decompression
author: ontology-spider-and-rea-learning-wave

edges.description: lyogavin/airllm at commit af3c212c52ebecad95f0d25eb2595e82988d0cdd; surfaced by Ontology-Spider and inspected via REA pyc_code facet
Complements TPU/XLA weight-gathered transformer inference partitioning with single-GPU disk-streaming bounds

claims.assertion: AirLLMBaseModel instantiates Hugging Face models on the meta device (init_empty_weights), strips compressed-tensors model-wide ct_decompress_hook before forward, and decompresses packed MXFP4 weight_packed/weight_scale tensors on-GPU per layer after PCIe transfer (4x less PCIe traffic), while capping host pin_memory() at max_pinned_layer_bytes = 2 GiB to prevent 2-in-flight MoE layers from locking ~34 GiB RAM.

AirLLMKimiK3 overrides layer_names_dict with expert_prefix (block_sparse_moe.experts) and small resident submodules so only routed sparse MoE experts (~16 of 896 per token, ~1 GB vs ~55 GB full layer) are streamed on demand.

distilled_learning: When streaming giant transformer/MoE checkpoints within tight VRAM budgets, keep packed weights compressed across PCIe and decompress on-device per layer, stream individual active MoE experts instead of full layers, and bound pinned host memory per in-flight layer (<= 2 GiB) with pageable fallback.
